editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(H\) and \(G\) be graphs. We say that \(G\) is \(H\)-colorable if there is a homomorphism \(c:G\to H\). If for all further homomorphisms \(c'\): \(G\to H\) there is \(f\in\Aut H\) such that \(c'=f\circ c\), then \(G\) is said to be uniquely \(H\)-colorable. A core is a graph having no homomorphisms to any of its proper subgraphs. The following theorems are proved by the help of probabilistic methods. (1) If the graph \(H\) is not \(H'\)-colorable, then for each integer \(g\geq 3\) there is a graph \(G\) of girth at least \(g\) which is \(H\)-colorable but not \(H'\)-colorable. (2) If \(H\) is a core, then for each integer \(g\geq 3\) there is a graph \(G\) of girth at least \(g\) which is uniquely \(H\)-colorable. A vertex-coloring \(c\) of a graph \(G\) by \(\{0,1,\dots,k-1\}\) is said to be a \((k,d)\)-coloring if \(d\leq|c(x)-c(y)|\leq k-d\) whenever the vertices \(x\) and \(y\) are adjacent. The star-chromatic number of \(G\) is defined as the infimum \(\chi^*(G)\) of the ratio \({k\over d}\) for all pairs \((k,d)\) for which there is a \((k,d)\)-coloring of \(G\). The graph \(G^k_d\) has vertices \(\{0,1,\dots,k-1\}\) and \((i,j)\) is an edge if and only if \(d\leq|i-j|\leq k-d\). This graph was defined in \textit{A. Vince} [J. Graph Theory 12, No. 4, 551-559 (1988; Zbl 0658.05028)], who observed that a graph \(G\) is \((k,d)\)-colorable if and only if \(G\) is homomorphic to \(G^k_d\). In the paper under review, it is observed that \(G^k_d\) is a core. Moreover, the following is proved. (3) If a graph \(G\) is uniquely \(G^k_d\)-colorable then \(\chi^*(G)=k/d\).


Correction: The definition of \(G^k_d\) was missed in the paper, but can easily be found in the references.

title.title: On sparse graphs with given colorings and homomorphisms.

editorial_contributions.text: Suppose that \(G=(V,E)\) is a graph and \(k,d\) are positive integers with \(k\geq 2d\) and \((k,d)=1\). A \((k,d)\)-coloring of \(G\) is a mapping \(f:V\rightarrow \{0,1,\ldots, k-1\}\) such that for every edge \(xy\in E\), min\(\{|f(x)-f(y)|, k-|f(x)-f(y)|\}\geq d\). In this paper the following property is constructively proved: If \(k\geq 3d-2, (k,d)=1\), \(A\) is a finite set and \(f_{1},\ldots ,f_{n}\) are mappings from \(A\) to \(\{0,1,\ldots ,k-1\}\), then for any integer \(l\), there is a graph \(G=(V,E)\) of girth at least \(l\) with \(A\subset V\), such that \(G\) has exactly \(n\) \((k,d)\)-colorings \(g_1,\dots, g_n\) (up to a permutation of the colors), and each \(g_{i}\) is an extension of \(f_{i}\). This result generalizes a result of \textit{V. Müller} who proved this for \(k\)-colorings [Discrete Math. 26, No. 2, 165-176 (1979; Zbl 0407.05037)]. Note that for \(n=1\), the method presented in this paper gives a construction of uniquely \((k,d)\)-colorable graphs. Some other results about the projectivity of the graphs \(G_{d}^{k}\) defined in the paper are also presented.

title.title: Construction of sparse graphs with prescribed circular colorings

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: A graph \(G\) is uniquely \(k\)-colorable if the chromatic number of \(G\) is \(k\) and every two \(k\)-colorings of \(G\) produce the same partition of the vertex set into \(k\) independent subsets (color classes). In this paper, we investigate the existence of triangles in uniquely 3-colorable graphs on surfaces. It is proved by \textit{G. Chartrand} and \textit{D. P. Geller} [J. Comb. Theory 6, 271--278 (1969; Zbl 0175.50206)] that any uniquely 3-colorable planar graph with at least four vertices contains at least two triangles, and by \textit{V. A. Aksionov} [Discrete Math. 20, 209--216 (1978; Zbl 0381.05028)] that if the number of vertices is at least five, then the uniquely 3-colorable planar graph contains at least three triangles. On the other hand, for surfaces \(F^2\) with non-positive Euler characteristic, there exist uniquely 3-colorable graphs on \(F^2\) without any triangle, which are constructed by \textit{C.-Y. Chao} and \textit{Z. Chen} [ibid. 112, No. 1--3, 21--27 (1993; Zbl 0780.05021)]. We prove that any uniquely 3-colorable graph on the projective plane contains at least one triangle. Furthermore, we report the finiteness of uniquely 3-colorable graphs on surfaces with high girth and a sufficient condition for the uniquely 3-colorability of graphs on surfaces.

title.title: Semistrong edge colorings of planar graphs

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: A natural digraph analogue of the graph-theoretic concept of an `independent set' is that of an `acyclic set', namely a set of vertices not spanning a directed cycle. Hence a digraph analogue of a graph coloring is a decomposition of the vertex set into acyclic sets and we say a digraph is uniquely \(n\)-colorable when this decomposition is unique up to relabeling. It was shown probabilistically in [\textit{A. Harutyunyan} et al., Can. J. Math. 64, No. 6, 1310--1328 (2012; Zbl 1254.05057)] that there exist uniquely \(n\)-colorable digraphs with arbitrarily large girth. Here we give a construction of such digraphs and prove that they have circular chromatic number \(n\). The graph-theoretic notion of `homomorphism' also gives rise to a digraph analogue. An acyclic homomorphism from a digraph \(D\) to a digraph \(H\) is a mapping \(\phi: V(D) \rightarrow V(H)\) such that \(uv \in A(D)\) implies that either \(\phi(u)\phi(v) \in A(H)\) or \(\phi(u)=\phi(v)\), and all the `fibers' \(\phi^{-1}(v)\), for \(v \in V(H)\), of \(\phi\) are acyclic. In this language, a core is a digraph \(D\) for which there does not exist an acyclic homomorphism from \(D\) to a proper subdigraph of itself. Here we prove some basic results about digraph cores and construct highly chromatic cores without short cycles.
